he kinetic mo lec u lar theory of matter asserts that the macroscopic properties of matter are determined by the structures of its constituent mol e cules and the interactions between them. Starting in the latter half of the 19th century, scien­ tists have developed a magnifi cent theoretical structure called statistical mechanics to explain the connection between microscopic structure and macroscopic proper­ ties. Statistical mechanics provides this bridge for all types of matter, ranging from biological ma te rials to solid­state integrated circuits. Today, every student of sci­ ence must be familiar with the concepts that make this connection. We give a quali­ tative introduction to these concepts, and apply them to numerous cases in the next four chapters.
